missionText: Our mission is to inspire, inform, educate, and entertain humanity — all from the comfort of your very own stall.
humorBody: A couple of New Jersey hunters are out in the woods when one of them falls to the ground. His friend calls 911. The operator calmly says, ‘First, make sure he is dead.’ There is silence, then a shot. The guy returns and says, ‘Okay, now what?’
mainFeatureBody:
The product you are seeing for the first time was first conceived eleven years ago. Before that, the idea was only a piece of paper, a criminal record, and a promise that something useful could be created from a difficult season. Since then, the vision has grown into a simple monthly publication designed for one place everyone eventually visits: the restroom.

After being in more than 300 cities over the past decade, one lesson keeps showing up: the pursuit of love and righteousness yields life, prosperity, and honor.
secondaryFeatureBody:
The box chair was originally invented by Billy Bryant, a US Air Force Special Forces veteran. After leaving the service, Billy studied mechanical design and went to work for a cardboard factory. One day, he built a cardboard box into a practical chair that could support more than 300 pounds.

Years later, the product became part of a wider event and advertising story: useful ideas can be simple, portable, and surprisingly memorable.
